quest.title: The Toy War: An Armistice
quest.description: Will the battle between clockwork workshop and clock shop, the wall between two brothers, dissolve when the two bosses meet? Or will the conflict grow more intense?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Enigmatic Copper Mainspring x70, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Haven't gone back, have you? Well, I must thank you — I'm sure father would be pleased that my brother and I finally spoke.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I see you're doing well, Caron.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: B—Brother? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: We haven't seen each other in so long, and THAT'S what you chose to say?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I—I just didn't expect you to come over to see me. I mean, our shops are quite close together, but you never came over. I thought you were still angry with me...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I'm not here to talk to you about what happened before. I'm just going to ask you this: that adventurer toy was made because of me, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Ah? Uh... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I knew I wouldn't be able to hide anything from you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, now Paimon's confused. Wasn't that toy inspired by Bennett?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Ah, I see you two have arrived as well... I'm sorry for not explaining previously, but I didn't know where to begin...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Although that adventurer did give me critical inspiration, my brother was the real reason I insisted on having the toy made.

choices.text: I can see why it might be complicated for you.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Caron, your mawkishness hasn't changed one bit.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: You haven't changed either, brother. I'm more and more convinced that you and that adventurer are the same type of person.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I don't have a Vision, nor am I an adventurer.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: But you have that same adventurous spirit. Bennett lives in an adventure, while you live for adventure.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Did you pick that flattery up from me too?

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: How can that be? You've never been a flatterer — you've never hesitated to tell me that I haven't any fighting spirit. And while the truth is frustrating, it is the truth nonetheless.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: You've always been trying to be the best toy merchant ever, but I acceded to the family's arrangements, continuing the cycle of clockmaking.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: Only people like you and Bennett could turn their passions into their profession. I cannot — it would take a hundred of me to match your courage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, don't say that about yourself!

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: There's no point in hiding this... When my brother first stated his intentions to move his shop next to mine, my first reaction was to consider moving the shop. Father would be ashamed, and rightly so.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: But in the end, the Northland Bank took that spot and separated us. A happy coincidence again, you could say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Arbon told us about it.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Hmph. Do you really think the world is so full of happy coincidences? That the Northland Bank just so happened to come between us at that time?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you mean, Livre?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I had reserved that spot long ago, but a new idea struck me, and so I transferred it to them for a low price. This didn't just come out of nowhere, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you were the one who got them involved! Huh. Did you think that your previous decision was too impulsive or something?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Ever since I left, my goal has always been to be the greatest toy merchant. But what sort of greatness would that be if the family feud made my brother move away in the process, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, that smells like concern to Paimon! You were just making excuses when you said you wanted Caron to apologize, weren't you?

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: A—Apologize?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: What "apologize"? Did I ever say that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's a really earnest denial, considering that you actually did say it!

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Hmph. I'm here to congratulate you, Caron. That toy... is quite well-made.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: Heh. It's been such a long time since I last heard a word of praise from you, brother. I didn't think that...

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I've also brought you a gift: here's the data I had these two adventurers gather over the last few days. This should help you create something even more interesting.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: Huh? But weren't you going to make toy Champion Duelists? That data's important to you, isn't it?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: That plan's suspended. The market shifted faster than I thought, so some ad-hoc adjustments will be necessary.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: But... This data... How could I just take it?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: You take it when I give it to you, obviously!

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: *sigh* In that case, I'll take it... for safe-keeping. Feel free to reclaim it, should you ever need it again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so Livre's "other plan" was to give the data to his brother.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I apologize, dear customers, that I did not ask for your suggestions first before doing this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, it's fine. You paid us, didn't you? And this is your personal matter. This was totally worth it if your relationship with your brother can be improved, right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Our thoughts are aligned in this, indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. Guess this was a successful third party intervention!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right. Livre, Caron, since we're all here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't you strike while the iron's hot and work together on something? You're good at making stuff, Caron, and we can have Livre do the advertising! If you do it as a team, it's sure to work out!

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I appreciate your good intentions, but there's no need.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: Hmm... I feel the same way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so this is what you two are gonna agree on!?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: That Bennett fellow said this too, didn't he? "The world is full of all sorts of people."

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: So you did remember that part.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: "The world is full of all sorts of people, and they all have sights that only they can see." If I learned anything from him at all, this would be it.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Caron and I are just different people, which is why we've set out on different paths. Perhaps he thinks that my path is too adventurous, and I for my part can't stand the kind of placid existence he leads.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: That's right. If the hour hand does the minute hand's work, it will get fired without compensation the next day.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: And while intense challenges are an adventure, is a simple life not one as well? Everyone's on their own journey of adventure.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: So, since we've each chosen our direction, let's walk down that path and seek our own unique sights.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: And I'll occasionally go meet with you. After all, your road will be quite difficult.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Pfft, don't you worry about me. At least I know how to enlist third parties to help me out of jams. I didn't sit around waiting for these adventurers or the Northland Bank, let me tell you that.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: And what will you do when there's a problem that even a third-party can't solve? I'm sure you know how the stiffer a gear is, the less durable it will be. I worry that...

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: And if we meet, we'll meet! What else can we do, huh? That's just life.

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: No. You won't be defeated by life, just like Bennett. And if things prove otherwise...

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Yeah?

response.speaker: Caron
response.text: I'll send you flying with a knuckle sandwich.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Hah, brat, listen to yourself, talking to your big brother like that. Don't get too cocky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if Lady Furina can sit at the judges' desk for a while, then a little brother can borrow his big brother's lines, right?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Haha, I see you're figuring us Fontainians out. I'd like to ask you something, so if you're free, let's meet outside my shop later.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: That's all I have to say today, Caron. I'll be heading back now.

choices.text: I don't really get what was so difficult about all this.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: That's on my brother for twisting himself about into loops over everything.

talks.objective: Talk to Livre, the shop owner

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you seem to be in a good mood.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Thanks to your help. Speaking of which, Caron's trip to Mondstadt gave me an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should go travel around for a bit and find some inspiration for toys myself.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: You've traveled the world. You probably know some friends like that Bennett. Do you have any suggestions for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we do have a lot of friends, but when it comes to toy inspiration, that might be a bit tough...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why not look for a third party?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? We're a valid third party, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Are you referring to... the Northland Bank?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you meant the previous third party! Oh, let Paimon think... The Northland Bank's under the Fatui, and the Fatui are under...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Are you referring to a Harbinger? Do you mean that we can make a toy themed after a Harbinger?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Huh! {NICKNAME}, do you mean... Oh, Paimon gets it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Livre, did you know that there's a very special Harbinger, whom they call the—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The greatest toy salesman in Snezhnaya"!

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: What? Is there such a person?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course, and he's a real expert, too! Maybe he'll inspire you... and y'know, a toy merchant and a seller would make a pretty awesome combo, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Thanks for your suggestions — they've been very helpful.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I don't think it would be easy to get in contact with a Harbinger, but I do have some connections at the Northland Bank. I'll see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. Don't forget to invite us to try whatever new toy you come up with!

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I will. Keep an ear out for news from me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, today's supposed to be the day when Livre's gonna go pay Caron a visit. Should we go have a look? It sure would be nice if they could make up...
